text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- The cabinet yesterday appointed eight persons to the State Privatisation and Holding Co. board of directors. State Audit Office chief Arpad Kovacs was named board chairman. @
- A report on the bank consolidation programme of 1992-1995 approved yesterday by the cabinet found a number of mistakes and irregularities in the process.
- The assets statements of Free Democrat MPs are accessible to all visitors at the MPs' office building as of yesterday, party president Ivan Peto announced.
- Judit Csiha, nominee for the post of privatisation minister and Szabolcs Fazekas for the minister of industry, trade and tourism were approved by parliamentary committees. @

- The Central Crime Fighting Directorate and a special parliamentary commission continued the investigation of the privatisation scandal. Meanwhile, authorities have sequestered property belonging to lawyer Marta Tocsik.

- Budapest police are questioning neo-Nazi Albert Szabo after it was established that remarks made at an October 23 rally by Szabo, head of the Hungarian People's Welfare Federation, could be interpreted as an incitement against a community. Szabo urged that Hungarian Jews be sent to Israel in his speech. @

- A study by US investment bank Shearson Lehman Brothers says the Magyar Hitel Bank is worth a symbolic HUF 1 under current Hungarian circumstances, according to a report in the Austrian weekly Wirtschaftswoche.
- One-time US national security adviser Zbigniew Brzezinski said on CNN that the US and the West are morally responsible for what happened after the 1956 Uprising in Hungary was crushed. @

- Hungarian Television was unable to come up with the broadcasting rights to the return leg of the Newcastle vs. Ferencvaros UEFA Cup encounter next Tuesday, so Hungarian soccer fans will be unable to watch a televised broadcast.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- The Supervisory Board of the State Privatisation and Holding Co. Thursday delivered a report on the Tocsik case saying responsibility rests with the privatisation minister, the board of directors, the chairman of the board, the general director, the deputy general director and the senior legal counsellor. @
- Westel 900 GSM projects a turnover of HUF 34 billion for this year, 70 per cent up on last year.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Hungary will host a symposium October 29-30 to assess the experiences of NATO Partnership for Peace countries in the Bosnian peace effort.
- The second Austrian consulate in Hungary opened in Szombathely earlier this week.
- Exports in the first eight months totalled HUF 1,231.5 billion, while a total of HUF 1,529.8 billion was imported into the country, the Central Statistics Office reports. @
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Unicbank, Postabank and two foreign companies have expressed interest in buying Mezobank.
-The Hungarian technical engineering company GEA-EGI signed a $30 million agreement to deliver ventilating cooling systems to a Turkish power plant.

- Gabor Szeles, president of bus maker Ikarus, signed a HUF 4 billion agreement on the delivery of 250 buses to Russia and an agreement on the delivery of 70 buses to Ikarus' British partner Hughes DAF to a total value of 3,5 million.
